outcomes.text: Distinguish monosaccharides, disaccharides and polysaccharides.
Recall the structures of alpha and beta glucose and of ribose.
Explain how condensation forms glycosidic bonds in disaccharides and polysaccharides, and how hydrolysis splits them.
Relate the structures of glucose, starch, glycogen and cellulose to their functions.
Describe how a triglyceride forms by ester bonds between glycerol and three fatty acids.
Compare saturated and unsaturated lipids.
Link lipid structure to energy storage, waterproofing and insulation.
Explain how phospholipid structure suits cell membranes.
Draw the general structure of an amino acid.
Explain how peptide bonds form polypeptides by condensation.
Describe the role of ionic, hydrogen and disulfide bonds in protein structure.
Explain how primary to quaternary structure determines properties of fibrous and globular proteins.
Relate the structures of collagen and haemoglobin to their functions.
Describe DNA structure: nucleotides, base pairing, backbones, phosphodiester and hydrogen bonds.
Explain semi-conservative replication and the roles of helicase, polymerase and ligase.
State that a gene is a base sequence coding for a polypeptide's amino acids.
Describe the structure of mRNA.
Describe the structure of tRNA including the anticodon.
Explain transcription in the nucleus and translation at the ribosome, with sense and anti-sense DNA.
Describe the genetic code: triplets, start and stop codons, degenerate, non-overlapping, non-coding DNA.
Define gene mutation using base deletion, insertion and substitution.
Explain how point mutations change amino acid sequences, as in sickle cell anaemia.
Describe enzymes as globular proteins.
Explain specificity and the induced fit hypothesis.
Explain that enzymes are catalysts lowering activation energy.
Explain how temperature, pH, substrate and enzyme concentration affect enzyme rate. Core practical 1.
Explain how initial rate is measured and why it matters.
Explain competitive, non-competitive and end-product inhibition.
Recognise that enzymes work both inside cells and outside them.
Explain the roles of nitrate, calcium, magnesium and phosphate ions in plants.
Explain how water's dipole and hydrogen bonding give high specific heat, solvent action, surface tension, incompressibility and density maximum at 4 C.

units.title: Topic 2: Cells, Viruses and Reproduction of Living Things

topics.title: 2.1 Eukaryotic and prokaryotic cell structure and function

outcomes.text: State cell theory: cells are the basic unit of structure, function and organisation.
Describe how cells are organised into tissues, organs and organ systems.
Describe prokaryotic ultrastructure: nucleoid, plasmids, 70S ribosomes, cell wall.
Distinguish Gram positive and negative walls and their antibiotic responses.
Describe eukaryotic ultrastructure and the functions of its organelles.
Explain how magnification and resolution are achieved in light and electron microscopy.
Explain why specimens are stained. Core practical 2: light microscope and micrometers.
Classify viruses by structure and nucleic acid type, using lambda phage, TMV, Ebola and HIV.
Describe the viral lytic cycle and latency.
Explain that viruses are not cells, so antivirals inhibit replication.
Explain why preventing spread is key to disease control, using the 2014 Ebola outbreak.
Evaluate the ethics of using untested drugs in epidemics.
Describe the regulated cell cycle: interphase, mitosis, cytokinesis.
Describe what happens to genetic material through the stages of mitosis.
Explain how mitosis supports growth, repair and asexual reproduction. Core practical 3: root tip squash.
Describe the stages of meiosis and how it produces haploid gametes.
Explain how independent assortment and crossing over create genetic variation.
Describe chromosome mutations such as translocation.
Explain how non-disjunction causes polysomy (Down's) and monosomy (Turner's).
Describe oogenesis and spermatogenesis.
Describe fertilisation from first contact to nuclear fusion.
Describe early embryo development to the blastocyst.
Describe formation of pollen grains in the anther and the embryo sac in the ovule.
Explain how male nuclei reach the embryo sac via the pollen tube. Core practical 4: sucrose and pollen tubes.
Describe double fertilisation forming a triploid endosperm and a zygote.
Recall the hierarchy from domain to species.
Discuss the limits of the species definition.
Explain why assigning organisms to species or finding new species is difficult.
Explain how gel electrophoresis distinguishes species and shows evolutionary relationships.
Recall that DNA sequencing and bioinformatics separate species and show relationships.
Explain how journals, peer review and conferences validate evidence for evolution.
Describe evidence for the three-domain model over five kingdoms and how scientists validated it.
Explain evolution by natural selection acting on variation to produce adaptations.
Explain how niches depend on physiological, behavioural and anatomical adaptations.
Explain how reproductive isolation leads to allopatric and sympatric speciation.
Describe the evolutionary race between pathogens and medicines.
Assess biodiversity by habitat species diversity index and by allele variety in a gene pool.
Explain the ethical and economic reasons for maintaining biodiversity.
Explain ex-situ and in-situ conservation and the issues with each.
Explain how surface area to volume ratio affects transport of molecules.
Explain why larger organisms need mass transport and specialised exchange surfaces.
Describe the fluid mosaic model of the cell surface membrane.
Explain diffusion, facilitated diffusion and osmosis as passive transport.
Explain how solubility, size and charge affect transport of molecules.
Describe endocytosis and exocytosis through vesicles. Core practicals 5 and 6: beetroot permeability, water potential.
Explain active transport and the role of ATP.
Explain that ADP phosphorylation takes energy and ATP hydrolysis supplies it.

subtopics.title: Gas exchange in animals and plants

outcomes.text: Explain gas exchange adaptations of insects, fish and mammals. Core practical 7: insect dissection.
Explain gas exchange in flowering plants: stomata, leaf surfaces, lenticels.
Describe the structure of heart, arteries, veins and capillaries.
Explain why double circulation beats single circulation in fish.
Describe the sequence of events in the cardiac cycle.
Explain myogenic stimulation via SAN, AVN and bundle of His.
Interpret ECG traces and cardiac pressure data.
Describe blood as plasma and cells including erythrocytes and the types of leucocyte.
Describe blood's roles in transport, defence, and forming lymph and tissue fluid.
Explain clotting: platelets, thromboplastin, prothrombin to thrombin, fibrinogen to fibrin.
Explain the stages of atherosclerosis, its health effects and risk factors.

topics.title: 4.5 Transport of gases in the blood

outcomes.text: Explain haemoglobin's role in carrying respiratory gases, including the Bohr effect.
Interpret the haemoglobin oxygen dissociation curve.
Compare haemoglobin with myoglobin.
Explain the higher oxygen affinity of fetal haemoglobin.

topics.title: 4.6 Transfer of materials between the circulatory system and cells

outcomes.text: Explain tissue fluid formation and reabsorption using hydrostatic and oncotic pressure.
Recall that unabsorbed tissue fluid returns to the blood through the lymph system.
Relate xylem and phloem structure to transport.
Explain apoplastic and symplastic water pathways.
Explain the cohesion-tension model of water transport.
Explain how temperature, light, humidity and air movement change transpiration. Core practical 8: potometer.
Evaluate the mass-flow hypothesis for phloem transport.
Explain that respiration makes ATP for metabolism and releases heat.
Name the stages: glycolysis, link reaction, Krebs cycle, oxidative phosphorylation.
Describe glycolysis: hexose phosphorylation by ATP, splitting to GP, and NADH and ATP production.
State that the link reaction and Krebs cycle occur in the mitochondrial matrix.
Explain how pyruvate oxidation releases carbon dioxide, NADH and ATP.
State that the electron transport chain sits in the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Explain how the electron transport chain generates ATP.
Explain oxygen as the final electron acceptor forming water.
Explain ATP synthesis by chemiosmosis.
Explain why mitochondrial membranes matter to the process.
Describe anaerobic respiration as partial hexose breakdown with low ATP yield.
Compare ATP yield per hexose in aerobic and anaerobic conditions.
Explain how lactate affects mammalian muscle contraction.
Explain ethanol formation in plant anaerobic respiration. Core practical 9: respirometer.
Explain absorption and action spectra. Core practical 10: wavelength and photosynthesis rate.
Explain why plants have several photosynthetic pigments. Core practical 11: chromatography.
Describe chloroplast structure: envelope, stroma, grana, lamellae.
Explain the role of thylakoid membranes in the light-dependent stage.
Explain cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation producing reduced NADP, ATP and oxygen.
Explain the role of the stroma in the light-independent stage.
Explain carbon dioxide fixation with RuBP and RUBISCO to form GP.
Explain how reduced NADP and ATP make GALP and regenerate RuBP.
Explain how GALP is used to make sugars, amino acids and other molecules.
Explain how carbon dioxide, light intensity and temperature limit photosynthesis.
Describe basic aseptic techniques for culturing organisms.
Explain the principles and techniques of culturing microorganisms.
Compare broth, agar and selective media. Core practical 13: streak plating.
Compare ways to measure bacterial growth: cell counts, dilution plating, mass, turbidity.
Describe growth curve phases and calculate exponential growth rate constants. Core practical 12.
Explain how bacteria infect by invading tissue and making toxins.
Distinguish exotoxins (Staphylococcus), endotoxins (Salmonella) and tissue invasion (TB).
Explain bactericidal and bacteriostatic action using penicillin and tetracycline.
Explain how antibiotic resistance develops and spreads.
Describe methods and difficulties in controlling antibiotic resistance.
Describe transmission, infection and effects of wheat stem rust, influenza virus and the malarial parasite.
Evaluate social, economic and ethical effects of malaria control methods and scientific validation.
Describe how macrophages, neutrophils and lymphocytes act.
Explain the humoral response: antigen-presenting T cells, T helpers, cytokines, B cells, clonal selection, plasma cells, antibodies.
Explain the cell-mediated response: antigen-presenting cells, T helpers, cytokines, T killers.
Explain T and B memory cells in the secondary response.
Distinguish natural, artificial, active and passive immunity.
Explain vaccination and herd immunity.
Discuss problems when some people choose not to vaccinate.
Define genome.
Explain PCR, and its uses in predicting protein sequences and genetic conditions, and in forensic profiling and paternity tests.
Recall that transcription factors are DNA-binding proteins.
Explain how transcription factors regulate gene expression.
Explain how RNA splicing gives different products from one gene.
Describe epigenetic change via non-coding RNA, histone modification and DNA methylation.
Recall that epigenetic modification drives cell differentiation.
Define stem cells and distinguish totipotent, pluripotent and multipotent.
Discuss medical opportunities and ethics of embryonic pluripotent stem cells.
Explain how epigenetic changes take totipotent cells to pluripotent to differentiated somatic cells.
Explain how fibroblasts are reprogrammed into iPS cells with named genes.
Explain why iPS cells are less problematic than embryonic stem cells.
Explain producing recombinant DNA with restriction endonucleases and DNA ligase.
Explain inserting recombinant DNA into cells using vectors such as viruses and gene guns.
Explain using antibiotic resistance marker genes and replica plating to find recombinant cells.
Explain how knockout mice reveal gene function.
Describe genetic modification of soya beans, including fatty acid changes to prevent oxidation.
Explain why GM crops and transgenic processes cause public debate.
Explain mutation as the source of new variation and how assortment and crossing over make new allele combinations.
Explain how random fertilisation adds variation.
Use the terms genotype, phenotype, homozygote, heterozygote, dominant, recessive, codominance, multiple alleles.
Construct genetic crosses and pedigree diagrams.
Explain inheritance of two non-interacting unlinked genes.
Explain autosomal linkage and cross results through meiosis, using Drosophila.
Explain X-linked inheritance, including haemophilia.
Use chi squared tests on observed and expected results.
Explain how stabilising and disruptive selection change allele frequencies and cause speciation.
Explain chance changes in allele frequency, including genetic drift.
Explain population bottlenecks and the founder effect.
Use the Hardy-Weinberg equation to track allele frequency change.
Define homeostasis as dynamic equilibrium.
Explain why pH, temperature and water potential must be kept steady.
Distinguish negative and positive feedback.
Explain hormone production by endocrine glands and action through target cell receptors.
Compare second-messenger action (adrenaline) with direct binding to transcription factors (oestrogen).
Describe auxins, cytokinins and gibberellins as plant growth substances. Core practical 14: gibberellin and amylase.
Describe auxin effects: cell elongation, apical dominance, root growth.
Explain interaction, such as antagonism of cytokinin and auxin on apical dominance.
Explain how phytochrome controls flowering and photomorphogenesis.

topics.title: 9.4 Structure and function of the mammalian nervous system

outcomes.text: Describe the central and peripheral nervous systems.
Describe the structure of the spinal cord.
Locate and give functions of medulla, cerebellum, cerebrum and hypothalamus.
Divide the peripheral system into autonomic and voluntary parts.
Explain the antagonistic sympathetic and parasympathetic systems.
Explain the resting potential from axon membrane properties and Na+ and K+ transport.
Explain how an action potential forms and propagates.
Explain faster myelinated conduction by saltatory conduction.
Describe synapse structure and function with acetylcholine and noradrenaline.
Explain excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic potentials.

topics.title: 9.6 Effects of drugs on the nervous system

outcomes.text: Explain drug effects on synapses: nicotine, lidocaine and cobra venom.
Describe the structure of the human retina.
Explain how rhodopsin starts action potentials.
Explain how rod and cone distribution supports vision across light levels.

topics.title: 9.8 Control of heart rate in mammals

outcomes.text: Explain autonomic heart rate control: baroreceptors, chemoreceptors, cardiac centre, noradrenaline and acetylcholine at the SAN.
Explain autonomic triggering of adrenaline release to raise heart rate.
Describe the gross and microscopic structure of the mammalian kidney.
Explain urea formation in the liver and removal by ultrafiltration.
Explain selective reabsorption in the proximal tubule and the loop of Henle as counter-current multiplier.
Explain ADH negative feedback via pituitary and hypothalamic osmoreceptors.
Explain kangaroo rat kidney adaptations to dry environments.
Distinguish endotherms from ectotherms.
Explain endotherm regulation by behaviour and autonomic control with thermoreceptors, hypothalamus and skin.
Define ecosystem and note they vary in size.
Define trophic levels.
Evaluate pyramids of numbers, biomass and energy, and how biomass and energy move.
Describe quadrats, transects, ACFOR, percentage cover and counts for abundance and distribution.
Choose suitable ecological techniques for a given ecosystem. Core practical 15: sampling methods.
Use t-test and Spearman rank correlation on ecological data.
Explain energy transfer using net and gross primary productivity.
Calculate transfer efficiency between trophic levels and explain energy losses.
Explain microorganisms' role in nutrient recycling.
Explain colonisation, succession and climax communities.
Explain how biotic and abiotic factors affect population size. Core practical 16: abiotic factor and distribution.
Interpret data on human impact: climate change and overfishing.
Explain the effect of treaties such as CITES on biodiversity.
Explain sustainability as managing human needs against conservation, using fish stocks and climate change.
Explain how journals, peer review and conferences validate climate change evidence.
